newsitem.title: USA: Cablevision declines comment on possible bids - NYT.
newsitem.headline: Cablevision declines comment on possible bids - NYT.

text.p: Cablevision Systems Corp's founder and chairman Charles Dolan declined to comment to the New York Times about possible bids for the company.

Cablevision, which owns a cable system with 2.8 million subscribers, sports teams and an array of entertainment assets, was not immediately available for comment. The New York Times published a story about Cablevision on Sunday.
Dolan has refused to dilute his family's holdings in the company and turned down a reported bid from Time Warner Inc - US West Media Group and a rumored offer from GTE Corp, the paper reported.
Cablevision's $3.1 billion of debt and $1.5 billion in preferred stock and the string of losses dating to 1993 have hurt the company's stock price, the paper said.
Walt Disney Co, News Corp Ltd and Liberty Media are reportedly speaking to Cablevision about investments, the paper said.
General Electric Co's NBC owns 25 percent of Cablevision's Rainbow Programming unit.
